events.title: Eastern Market — Weekend Market & Flea
events.description: Historic public market plus weekend outdoor flea, arts, and crafts. Live music when weather permits.

events.title: Capitol Hill Farmers Markets
events.description: Seasonal weekend farmers markets with local produce and vendors.

events.title: Lincoln Park
events.description: Large Capitol Hill green space with playground, paths, and statues. Dog-friendly. Cafes at both ends.

events.title: Garfield Park
events.description: Neighborhood park with playground, tennis, basketball, bocce, and a community garden.

events.title: Yards Park & Navy Yard Waterfront
events.description: Riverfront park with fountains, boardwalk, and frequent seasonal weekend programming.

events.title: National Mall & Smithsonian Museums
events.description: Free Smithsonian museums and monuments. Reliable all-weather, all-ages option.

events.title: United States Botanic Garden
events.description: Free conservatory and gardens at the foot of the Capitol, with a Children's Garden.

events.title: Anacostia Riverwalk Trail Ride
events.description: Paved riverfront trail for a family bike ride, with Capital Bikeshare access nearby.

events.title: The Fields at RFK — Community Open Play & Disc Golf
events.time: Open hours vary (8 AM–dusk disc golf)
events.venue: The Fields at RFK Campus (401 Oklahoma Ave NE)
events.description: Turf fields with community open-play hours plus DC's free disc golf course. 10-min walk from Stadium-Armory.

events.title: CHAW Gallery (Capitol Hill Arts Workshop)
events.venue: Capitol Hill Arts Workshop (545 7th St SE)
events.description: Rotating gallery shows of local artists, two blocks from Eastern Market. Check site for current exhibition.

events.title: Beetlejuice – The Musical (National Tour)
events.venue: The National Theatre, 1321 Pennsylvania Ave NW, Washington DC
events.description: The ghost with the most comes to DC in the acclaimed Broadway musical based on the classic Tim Burton film. A wildly funny, darkly quirky, and visually spectacular show.

events.title: Free Friday Concerts at Eastern Market Metro Park
events.venue: Eastern Market Metro Park, Capitol Hill
events.description: Every Friday in July starting July 3, free local music concerts are held at Eastern Market Metro Park. The series features diverse local DC acts — past performers include the DMV Music Academy steel pan ensemble and Moonscape (video game and anime soundtracks). Covers Fridays July 18 and July 25.

events.title: STC Academy Summer Repertory: Macbeth
events.venue: Shakespeare Theatre Company – Michael R. Klein Theatre, 450 7th St NW, Washington DC
events.price: Tickets discounted vs. mainstage; under-35 pricing available. Likely ~$25–$55.
events.description: Shakespeare's propulsive tragedy, directed by Alec Wild with astonishing puppetry by Ksenya Litvak. Performed by the STC Academy Class of 2026 as part of their MFA repertory showcase — classical work in its purest form.

events.title: STC Academy Summer Repertory: Twelfth Night
events.venue: Shakespeare Theatre Company – Michael R. Klein Theatre, 450 7th St NW, Washington DC
events.price: Tickets discounted vs. mainstage; under-35 pricing available. Likely ~$25–$55.
events.description: Directed by Jess Chayes, this is Shakespeare's most lyrical and enduring comedy — performed as the culmination of a year of classical training by the STC Academy Class of 2026. Runtime approximately 2 hrs 45 min with one intermission.

events.title: Pippin
events.venue: Signature Theatre, 4200 Campbell Ave, Arlington, VA
events.price: Varies; Signature offers under-30 and rush pricing. Likely $35–$95.
events.description: Stephen Schwartz's (Godspell, Wicked) musical masterpiece of purpose, ambition, lust, and glory, thrillingly staged by director Matthew Gardiner for summer at Signature Theatre.

events.title: What Became of Us
events.venue: Signature Theatre, 4200 Campbell Ave, Arlington, VA
events.price: Varies; Signature offers under-30 and rush pricing. Likely $35–$85.
events.description: A beautiful and moving play about two siblings striving for connection over the course of a lifetime — exploring memory, love, and what we leave behind.

events.title: Capitol Riverfront Friday Night Concert Series (14th Season)
events.description: The free Capitol Riverfront Friday Night Concert Series is back for its 14th season on the Yards Park boardwalk. Every Friday night this summer, come to Yards Park to enjoy the river view, fantastic bands, food and drinks, and restaurants within walking distance. Family-friendly with grassy open space. Covers Fridays July 18, July 25, and August 1.

events.title: Capitol Riverfront Saturday Farmers Market on Half Street
events.description: Weekly Saturday farmers market in the Capitol Riverfront neighborhood on Half Street, featuring over 30 unique vendors with fresh produce, poultry, and specialty goods. Runs every Saturday from 9:00 AM to 1:00 PM. Covers all three target Saturdays: July 18, July 25, and August 1.

events.title: Escape with Washington Improv Theater
events.time: Various (4:00 PM, 6:00 PM, 8:00 PM Saturdays; 9:00 PM Fridays)
events.description: Washington Improv Theater's summer series 'Escape with Washington Improv Theater' runs July 11–August 1 at Studio Theatre (1501 14th St NW). Performances are confirmed on Saturday Aug 1 at 4:00 PM, 6:00 PM, and 8:00 PM, and Friday Jul 31 at 9:00 PM. WIT's shows are completely unscripted and driven by audience suggestions. First four weeks in the Milton Theater, second half in the Shargai space.

events.title: Farmers Market SW at The Wharf
events.description: Weekly Saturday morning farmers market at M Street Landing outside Pitango, Philippe Chow, and Fish Shop at The Wharf. Features locally sourced food from regional farmers. Runs every Saturday through November. Covers all three target weekends (July 18, July 25, August 1).

events.title: Friday Evening Parades at Marine Barracks Washington (8th & I)
events.time: Fridays, evening (doors open before parade; check barracks.marines.mil for exact time)
events.venue: Marine Barracks Washington, 8th & I Streets SE
events.description: Every Friday from May through August, the historic Marine Barracks at 8th & I hosts a free 75-minute evening parade ceremony featuring the precision of the Marine Corps, performed by 'The President's Own' Marine Band, 'The Commandant's Own' Drum & Bugle Corps, and the renowned Silent Drill Platoon. Free to attend; advance tickets/reservations required. A spectacular and unique DC experience for all ages.

events.title: Eastern Market Outdoor Weekend Market
events.description: Every weekend, the streets and plazas surrounding Eastern Market come alive with farm-fresh produce vendors, handmade arts and crafts from local artists, live music, and food. Saturday outdoor market runs along 7th St SE from Pennsylvania Ave SE to North Carolina Ave SE through at least September 26, 2026. Covers all six target weekend days.

events.title: Mrs. Doubtfire (The Musical)
events.venue: Kennedy Center – Eisenhower Theater, 2700 F St NW, Washington DC
events.price: Varies; KC Millennium Stage offers free daily performances separately. Tickets from ~$50+. MyTix rush available for ages 18–30.
events.description: The internationally acclaimed hit musical based on the beloved film. Everyone's favorite Scottish nanny comes to the Kennedy Center in this hilarious and heartfelt family-friendly comedy.

events.title: The Fields at RFK Campus — Open Recreation Season
events.description: The Fields at RFK Campus, a 27-acre outdoor sports complex on the west bank of the Anacostia River with turf fields, bike paths, and a celebration pavilion, is open for its summer season (June 14 – August 29, 2026). Community play, organized league sports, and open recreational use are available. Note: RFK Stadium itself is under demolition and closed to the public.

events.title: The Municipal Fish Market at The Wharf
events.description: The nation's oldest continuously operating open-air fish market, located along the waterfront at The Wharf. Pick up fresh seafood including oysters on the half shell, blue crabs, and whole fish caught that morning. Open daily and especially lively on weekends.

events.title: Yards Park Water Features & Canal Basin
events.description: The water wall, dancing fountains, and canal basin at Yards Park are open daily from 10:00 AM to 8:00 PM all through September for all neighborhood visitors and residents. A free, family-friendly way to cool off on hot summer weekends along the Anacostia River waterfront.

events.title: CrazySexyCool – The TLC Musical
events.venue: Arena Stage (Kreeger Theater), 1101 6th St SW, Washington DC
events.price: Tickets vary; TodayTix rush/lottery likely available
events.description: World premiere semi-biographical musical about TLC — Tionne, Lisa 'Left Eye' Lopes, and Rozonda 'Chilli' Thomas — the most successful female group of all time. Charts their friendship, story, and legacy through their chart-topping music.

events.title: Something Rotten! (The Theatre Lab)
events.venue: Atlas Performing Arts Center, 1333 H St NE, Washington DC
events.price: Varies; The Theatre Lab productions typically ~$25–$50.
events.description: The Theatre Lab School of the Dramatic Arts stages this Tony-nominated musical comedy set in the Renaissance, where two brothers try to out-Shakespeare Shakespeare by writing the world's very first musical.

events.title: National Gallery of Art — Jazz in the Garden (Friday Evenings)
events.time: Fridays, evening (check nga.gov for exact times)
events.venue: National Gallery of Art Sculpture Garden
events.price: Free (food/drink available for purchase; alcohol requires 21+ ID)
events.description: The National Gallery of Art's beloved outdoor Friday-evening Jazz in the Garden concert series runs through August 14, 2026, with July performances on the 17th, 24th, and 31st. The concert takes place in the NGA Sculpture Garden on the National Mall. Admission is free; food and drinks are available for purchase (alcohol restricted to 21+, but families with teens are welcome to enjoy the garden atmosphere).

events.title: The Outsiders (The Musical)
events.venue: Kennedy Center – Opera House, 2700 F St NW, Washington DC
events.price: Varies; MyTix rush available for ages 18–30.
events.description: Winner of four Tony Awards® including Best Musical. Adapted from S.E. Hinton's seminal novel and Francis Ford Coppola's iconic film, this thrilling production makes its highly anticipated Washington DC debut.

events.title: The Notebook – The Musical (National Tour)
events.time: Various (7:30 PM evenings; matinees Sat/Sun 2:00 PM)
events.venue: The National Theatre, 1321 Pennsylvania Ave NW, Washington DC
events.price: Varies; avg ~$160–$230. TodayTix rush/lottery likely available.
events.description: Based on the best-selling Nicholas Sparks novel that inspired the iconic film, this moving musical tells the timeless love story of Noah and Allie across decades.

events.title: America 250 Scavenger Hunt — Learn Fun History Facts and Win a Prize!
events.venue: Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial Library — Central Library
events.description: A self-guided scavenger hunt at MLK Library tied to America's 250th anniversary celebrations. Kids and teens learn history facts and earn a prize upon completion. Part of DCPL's Discover Summer programming.

events.title: DCPL 'Just Your Imagination' Workshops with The Phillips Collection (Eight DCPL Locations)
events.time: Check dclibrary.libnet.info/events for specific branch dates/times
events.venue: Eight DC Public Library Neighborhood Branches (Multiple)
events.description: A partnership between DC Public Library and The Phillips Collection bringing free art workshops to eight DCPL branch locations during Discover Summer. Sessions encourage creative exploration and imagination-driven art-making for youth and teens. Check the DCPL events calendar for your nearest branch and weekend session times.

events.title: DCPL Discover Summer — Beginners Teen Crochet Class at Capitol View Library
events.time: Check dclibrary.libnet.info/events for specific session dates
events.description: A beginner-friendly crochet class specifically for teens, offered at Capitol View Neighborhood Library as part of DCPL's Discover Summer programming. No experience necessary. Check the DCPL events calendar for specific session dates across the covered weekends.

events.title: DCPL Discover Summer Library Day at National Museum of American History
events.description: DC Public Library is partnering with the National Museum of American History for a special Library Day as part of Discover Summer. Families can stop by the library's table inside the museum for fun activities, suggested reading lists, and giveaways. Registration recommended; check dclibrary.org/discover-summer for the specific date within the summer window.

events.title: Discover Summer — All-Ages Reading & Learning Program (DCPL)
events.venue: All DC Public Library Neighborhood Branches
events.description: DC Public Library's city-wide summer celebration of reading and learning, running June 1–Aug. 31. Participants pick up a Discover Summer Bingo Board at any neighborhood library or sign up online via Beanstack. Complete activities (reading, visiting museums, bringing a friend to the library) to earn prizes including Washington Nationals tickets. Teen-specific programming includes the Know Your Power Teen Art Contest and creative workshops in music, visual arts, and writing. Drop-in at your nearest branch.

events.title: Just Dance — Wednesday Afternoon Drop-In (Mt. Pleasant Library)
events.description: Drop-in Just Dance sessions on Wednesday afternoons throughout summer at Mt. Pleasant Neighborhood Library. Part of DCPL's Discover Summer programming — fun, active, and free for all ages.

events.title: Lego Social at Bellevue (William O. Lockridge) Neighborhood Library
events.description: Drop-in Lego Social sessions at Bellevue Library — create, engineer, and make new friends. Part of DCPL's Discover Summer programming and open to kids and tweens. Check the online events calendar for exact weekend dates.

events.title: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum — Free Admission with New Exhibits
events.description: The Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum, celebrating its 50th anniversary in 2026, features five new exhibits this year. Visitors can explore space, technology, and World War II history with interactive galleries and artifacts. All Smithsonian museums on the National Mall are free to enter. Great for teens interested in science, aviation, and space exploration.

events.title: Smithsonian National Museum of American History — 'In Pursuit of Life, Liberty & Happiness' Exhibition
events.description: The Smithsonian's National Museum of American History is leading the nation's 250th-anniversary celebrations with this bold, immersive exhibition exploring the ideals of the Declaration of Independence. The exhibit traces how Americans have pursued the promises of life, liberty, and happiness. DC Public Library has a special presence here during Library Days, with a table for fun activities and suggested reading lists. Free admission; no tickets required.

events.title: Summer Games for Teens — Beat the Heat with Blips and Bytes
events.venue: Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial Library — Central Library
events.description: Drop-in gaming and tech activities for teens at the MLK Central Library throughout summer 2026 as part of Discover Summer programming. Teens can cool off and engage with video games, digital activities, and more in an all-ages, welcoming environment.

events.title: Teen Anime Club — Let's Watch and Talk About Anime!
events.venue: Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial Library — Central Library
events.description: Ongoing summer anime watch-and-discuss club for teens at MLK Library as part of Discover Summer programming. Drop in to watch anime and join discussions with other teen fans.

events.title: US Botanic Garden — 'Fierce Flora: Tales of Survival and Demise' Exhibition
events.time: Regular garden hours (10 am–5 pm daily)
events.description: Ongoing free multisensory exhibit at the US Botanic Garden exploring the ferocious side of the plant world — from carnivorous plants to toxic species. The exhibit explains how plants have evolved unique survival features to defend against herbivores, infection, and competitors, and how plant-derived chemicals are used in medicine. Open daily; no tickets required.

events.title: District Vibes / American Pride: How DC Changed American Culture — Exhibition
events.venue: Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial Library — Central Library
events.description: Free exhibit at MLK Central Library (with satellite locations across the city) through Sept. 27 exploring DC's vibrant cultural contributions to American life — from the football huddle to the modern blood bank to legends like Marvin Gaye. Features images, artifacts, storytelling, and free programs.

events.title: US Botanic Garden — 'America's State Flowers: An America250 Celebration' Exhibition
events.time: Regular garden hours (10 am–5 pm daily)
events.description: Free outdoor and indoor exhibition at the US Botanic Garden celebrating America's 250th anniversary by showcasing the official state flowers of all 50 states and US territories. Varieties include fragrant magnolias, roses, orchids, bluebonnets, and saguaro cactus flowers. Open through October 12, 2026. The garden's Children's Garden is also open for 2026, inviting families to explore, dig, plant, and water.

events.title: DC Improv Showcase Weekend – Benny Nwokeabia & Lineup
events.description: DC Improv weekend showcase featuring Benny Nwokeabia, Amber Hendrix, Tyler Horvath, Apple Brown Betty, and Matty Litwack. The Jul 24–26 run is confirmed on the official DC Improv Seat Engine calendar; Jul 18–19 falls within that same multi-night engagement. Showcases run ~90 minutes. 18+ with a 2-item food/drink minimum.

events.title: Girls Rock! DC July Summer Camp Showcase
events.description: Summer camp showcase from Girls Rock! DC featuring youth performers. A family-friendly, community-oriented afternoon concert event.

events.title: Hains Point Hoopla + Picnic Potluck Bike Ride
events.venue: Hains Point Picnic Area A, East Potomac Park
events.description: Come out to Hains Point to celebrate this beloved public space. Enjoy the park, meet neighbors, share food at a picnic potluck, and bike, run, or walk as many loops as you'd like around the point. A community outdoor gathering with cycling at its heart.

events.title: Right Round – 80s Alt Pop Dance Party
events.description: 80s alternative and pop dance party night at the Black Cat Red Room. Late-night bar event.

events.title: Smithsonian Sleepover at the National Museum of Natural History
events.price: Paid — see smithsonianassociates.org for registration price
events.description: An overnight adventure inside the National Museum of Natural History for children ages 8–14 and their adult chaperones. Guests wander through the Fossil Hall, explore Earth's past and ocean wonders, and play 'The Game of Survival' — making underwater fossils, building dinosaurs, and learning to eat like a T-Rex. Includes hands-on crafts and guided gallery games. Additional NMNH sleepover dates: July 31 and Aug. 14.

events.title: So Fetch – 2000s Dance Party
events.description: High-energy 2000s pop and alt dance party tribute act. A fun, accessible night for all ages at DC's legendary U Street club.

events.title: Ward 5 Family Biking + DC Bike Party Summer Ride
events.venue: Ward 5, Washington DC (exact start TBA — check waba.org)
events.description: A joint community ride co-hosted by Ward 5 Family Biking and DC Bike Party. Billed as their 'funnest ride & party yet,' this family-friendly group ride is open to all ages and experience levels. Past Ward 5 Family Biking rides have started at neighborhood rec centers and parks in NE DC. Check waba.org and ward5familybiking.org for the confirmed start location.

events.title: Riverfront (Re)Connect: Community Kayaking on the Anacostia
events.description: The Capitol Riverfront BID has partnered with Ballpark Boathouse to offer community kayaking along the Anacostia River as part of the Riverfront (Re)Connect Summer Series. Participants enjoy an hour of paddling with neighbors at a discounted rate. July 21 is one of two confirmed dates (the other is August 18).

events.title: Sunset Cinema: Catch Me If You Can (2002)
events.description: Free outdoor Wednesday movie screening on Transit Pier at The Wharf, presented by Pacifico Beer. Film: Catch Me If You Can (2002). Doors/seating open at 7:00 PM; film begins at 7:30 PM. Limited Adirondack chairs on first-come first-served basis; blankets and folding chairs welcome. Family-friendly; dogs on leash welcome.

events.title: Rock the Dock: The Fearless Eras (Taylor Swift Tribute)
events.description: Free Friday night concert on the Floating Stage at Transit Pier featuring The Fearless Eras, a Taylor Swift tribute band. Part of the all-summer Rock the Dock series presented by Pacifico Beer. Genres include pop and country. Bring a blanket or chair; food available from Wharf restaurants and the stageside kiosk.

events.title: Smithsonian Sleepover at the American History Museum (Girl Scout Only)
events.price: Paid — see smithsonianassociates.org for registration price
events.description: Exclusive Girl Scout-only overnight at the National Museum of American History. Guests take an 'All-American Road Trip' through the museum's galleries, exploring the America 250 exhibit 'In Pursuit of Life, Liberty & Happiness,' playing I-Spy and the license plate game, and becoming presidential candidates in a memorable overnight adventure.

events.title: Holy Rollers with Hammered Hulls and The Owners
events.description: Punk/rock showcase headlined by DC legends Holy Rollers, with Hammered Hulls and The Owners supporting. A classic underground DC rock night.

events.title: Jackie Kashian at DC Comedy Loft
events.description: Stand-up comedian Jackie Kashian performs at the DC Comedy Loft (1523 22nd St NW). Shows confirmed for July 23–25 on multiple aggregator calendars. Two-item minimum per person in the showroom.

events.title: Rahill
events.description: Rahill (of Jhené Aiko's background) performs solo at the 9:30 Club. Indie R&B and ethereal vocals in an intimate club setting.

events.title: Sheryl Underwood at DC Improv
events.description: Emmy-award-winning comedian and co-host of 'The Talk' Sheryl Underwood headlines at DC Improv. Multiple shows confirmed across the Jul 24–26 weekend on aggregator and washington.org listings. 18+ with a 2-item food/drink minimum.

events.title: Taylor Williamson at Arlington Cinema & Drafthouse
events.description: Comedian Taylor Williamson performs at Arlington Cinema & Drafthouse (2903 Columbia Pike, Arlington, VA). Multiple shows confirmed for Jul 24–26 weekend on aggregator listings. Tickets typically $18–$28 per the venue's stated price range. 21+ unless accompanied by a parent.

events.title: Tour de Francs — C3 Chesapeake Cycling Club (via WABA)
events.venue: Ridgely, MD (exact start location TBA — check waba.org/fun)
events.description: A no-cost 26-mile community ride hosted by C3 Chesapeake Cycling Club, listed on WABA's events calendar. Features a strawberry shortcake pit stop along the route and a post-ride celebration with hotdogs and BBQ. Relaxed, all-paces-welcome atmosphere.

events.title: Sunset Cinema: Apollo 13 (1995)
events.description: Free outdoor Wednesday movie screening on Transit Pier at The Wharf, presented by Pacifico Beer. Film: Apollo 13 (1995). Doors/seating open at 7:00 PM; film begins at 7:30 PM. Limited Adirondack chairs on first-come first-served basis; blankets and folding chairs welcome. Family-friendly; dogs on leash welcome.

events.title: Rock the Dock: 7 Deadlies (Rock / Pop Covers)
events.description: Free Friday night concert on the Floating Stage at Transit Pier featuring 7 Deadlies, a pop and rock cover band. Part of the Rock the Dock series presented by Pacifico Beer. Seating is limited; food and drinks available from Wharf restaurants.

events.title: Souls of Mischief
events.description: Oakland hip-hop legends Souls of Mischief perform at Union Stage. Known for classic 90s rap including '93 'Til Infinity.

events.title: ALL THE FEELINGS TOUR: Metric, Broken Social Scene & Stars
events.description: A landmark Canadian indie-rock triple bill: Metric, Broken Social Scene and Stars co-headline the All The Feelings Tour at The Anthem.

events.title: Lincoln Theatre – Saturday Night Show (Aug 1)
events.description: Live music at the historic Lincoln Theatre on U Street. Artist TBA — confirmed show slot with GA standing ($15.50) and balcony seats ($28.25) on sale.

events.title: Max Meisel at DC Comedy Loft – Cellar Loft Debut
events.description: Max Meisel makes his Cellar Loft Debut at the DC Comedy Loft. Meisel is an LA-based comedian currently featuring on Tom Arnold's 'My Crazy X-Wife' tour, and producer of BackDoor Comedy. Run confirmed for July 31–August 1 on the official DC Comedy Loft events page. Two-item minimum per person.

events.title: RenRiot and Gina Young
events.description: RenRiot and Gina Young perform at the Black Cat. Independent and alternative artists on DC's storied U Street corridor.

events.title: United We Dance
events.description: Dance music showcase at the 9:30 Club. Electronic and dance-oriented acts in DC's most iconic mid-size venue.

events.title: Sunset Cinema: Roman Holiday (1953)
events.description: Free outdoor Wednesday movie screening on Transit Pier at The Wharf, presented by Pacifico Beer. Film: Roman Holiday (1953). Doors/seating open at 7:00 PM; film begins at 7:30 PM. Limited Adirondack chairs on first-come first-served basis; blankets and folding chairs welcome. Family-friendly; dogs on leash welcome.

events.title: Rock the Dock: Salsa Dance Night with Cubano Groove
events.description: Free Friday themed dance night on Transit Pier combining live salsa music by Cubano Groove with instruction by Salsa with Silvia. Part of the Rock the Dock series presented by Pacifico Beer. One of several themed dance nights on select Fridays this summer where each night features a different style of music and dancing.

events.title: KALEO – Way Down We Go Tour (with Dogpark)
events.description: Icelandic blues-rock powerhouse KALEO brings their Way Down We Go Tour to The Anthem, with indie-rock opener Dogpark.

events.title: Lincoln Theatre – Saturday Night Show (Aug 8)
events.description: Confirmed show slot at Lincoln Theatre on August 8. Artist TBA — doors 7:30 PM, show 8:30 PM. Check the official site for lineup updates.

events.title: National Zoo Elephant Day — DCPL Library Day
events.description: On Saturday, August 8, the Smithsonian's National Zoo celebrates Elephant Day — a celebration of Asian elephants and the Zoo's long-standing commitment to their care and conservation. DC librarians will host special storytimes, give away DC library swag, and share amazing book titles for kids and teens to check out. Registration opens July 10 on dclibrary.org/discover-summer.

events.title: Tommy Davidson at DC Improv
events.description: Tommy Davidson, known for countless unforgettable sketches on 'In Living Color,' headlines at DC Improv. Confirmed as an 'early August' engagement by dc-improv.ticketsfairfax.net and listed among the DC Improv's Jun–Dec 2026 headliner slate on washington.org. 18+ with 2-item minimum.

events.title: MLK Library Rooftop Punk Shows — Season 12 (August Date: Abacot, Girls on Toast + Guest)
events.venue: Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial Library — Rooftop
events.description: The MLK Library's legendary all-ages rooftop concert series returns for its 12th season, marking 50 years of punk in the United States. The August 12 show features Abacot, Girls on Toast, and a to-be-announced special guest. All performances are free and open to all ages — described as 'the most fun you will ever have at the library.' The first show of the season was July 8.

events.title: Argo and the Violet Queens with Massie, Cuni & Pink-house
events.description: Argo and the Violet Queens headline with supporting acts Massie, Cuni, and Pink-house. Independent and alternative music at Black Cat.

events.title: Howard Jones: Things Can Only Get Better Tour (with Wang Chung, The English Beat, Modern English & more)
events.description: A massive 80s new wave extravaganza featuring Howard Jones, Wang Chung, The English Beat, and Modern English. Multiple confirmed headliners on one bill.

events.title: Oh He Dead
events.description: Oh He Dead performs at the 9:30 Club. Genre-bending live act at DC's premier U Street concert club.
